page: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an arm64-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. The server features 2 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. It incorporates 64 KB of L1 instruction/data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, backed by 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, while omitting local instance storage.

Benchmark evaluation reveals high single-core performance alongside moderate overall throughput due to the low core count. The Neoverse-V3 architecture demonstrates top-tier single-threaded capability, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2306.0 and high single-threaded throughput in data compression tests, such as 36.49 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.21 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate multi-core metrics, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 4001.26 and a PassMark CPU score of 2838.84, rank lower relative to higher-core server classes. Memory bandwidth tests yielded uncached read speeds of 64.7 GB/sec, supporting steady database operations at 3998.55 operations per second in PassMark and 6.48 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance demonstrates strong cost efficiency for single-threaded workloads and light application duties where core-level compute speed matters more than multi-core parallel capacity. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and a modest total memory capacity of 4.0 GB, which restricts execution of memory-heavy tasks or large-scale machine learning models. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, small key-value caching, and microservices execution.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized arm64 instance powered by a 3.3 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no local storage. The server delivers strong single-core compute performance, highlighted by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression of 36.49 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 2306.0. Multi-core performance is limited by core count, though it maintains steady throughput in key-value operations like Redis SET at 6.48 million ops/sec and static web serving at 8.17 GB/sec. This instance offers efficient resource utilization for single-threaded data processing, lightweight web applications, microservices, and small key-value caching layers where single-core capability is paramount.
